description: a wildfire sensor sends a smoke alert to the dispatch center, which checks it against satellite images. if the satellite confirms a fire dispatch pages the duty ranger, otherwise it logs a false alarm and keeps watching the sensor. the ranger drives out and estimates the spread, and unless the wind is above forty kilometres an hour the ranger sends a ground crew. when the wind is too strong the ranger calls the regional command, which orders an evacuation through the county sheriff. the sheriff texts every resident in the zone, and residents who don't reply within ten minutes get a door knock from a deputy. once the crew contains the fire they report back to dispatch, which closes the incident.

errors.detail: The single wind condition is split into two decision boxes, 'Wind calm?' and 'Wind too strong?', that the ranger feeds unconditionally. Each has only a 'yes' edge, so the 'no' outcome (regional command or ground crew) is never drawn.

The ten-minute no-reply condition is written into the Resident to Deputy edge label instead of a decision box like 'Reply within ten minutes?'. As drawn, the deputy is reached from every resident, and the residents who do reply have no outcome.
A separate 'Fire Crew' box duplicates 'Ground Crew'. The text has the same crew contain the fire and report back, and the containment step is not shown.

The final step, dispatch closing the incident, is folded into the label of the crew-to-dispatch edge. Nothing shows dispatch closing the incident after the report, and the diagram otherwise dead-ends at Dispatch Center.
The ranger driving out and estimating the spread, which comes before the wind decision, is not shown as a step.

description: the transplant coordinator gets a donor kidney and runs it through the matching system. the matching system ranks waiting patients by blood type and tissue match and sends the top patient to the surgeon. if the surgeon accepts the organ the hospital calls the patient in, otherwise the matching system offers it to the next patient on the list. when the patient arrives the lab cross-matches their blood again and only if the cross-match is negative does the surgery go ahead, else the kidney goes back to the matching system. after surgery the recovery ward monitors the patient and pages the surgeon if creatinine rises.

errors.detail: There is no decision box for whether the surgeon accepts the organ. 'accepts organ?' is only an edge label from Surgeon to Hospital, and the 'otherwise offer to next patient' path is an unconditional Matching System -> Patient edge instead of a 'no' outcome.

The surgery step is missing and nothing leads to the Recovery Ward. After a negative cross-match the flow goes only to Surgeon, and the Recovery Ward has no incoming edge, so the 'after surgery' monitoring is disconnected.
The 'Creatinine high?' decision has a 'no' edge back to Matching System. The text describes no such outcome; it only says the ward pages the surgeon if creatinine rises.

description: telemetry from the satellite comes down through a ground station, and there is a decoder in front of the mission database. the decoder checks every frame's checksum and drops it if the checksum fails, otherwise it writes the frame to the mission database. an anomaly detector reads the database every minute and if a reading is out of range it alerts the flight controller. the flight controller decides whether it's a real fault; if it is they upload a safe-mode command back to the satellite through the ground station, if it isn't they mark the alert as noise. the database is replicated and uses round robin.

errors.detail: When the checksum fails ('yes'), the diagram sends the frame on to be written to the mission database. The text says a failed frame is dropped.
The 'no' (checksum passes) outcome is missing from the decision box, and there is no 'drop frame' step. The write to the database is not tied to the checksum passing.
There is no 'reading out of range?' decision. The Anomaly Detector alerts the Flight Controller unconditionally instead of only when a reading is out of range.
The safe-mode command upload is not shown. On a real fault the edge goes to Ground Station with no command step and no edge on to the satellite, and there is no Satellite box.
When the fault is not real ('no'), the diagram loops back to the Anomaly Detector. The text says the alert is marked as noise, and that step is missing.

description: a customer files a car insurance claim in the app, and the app sends it to the claims service. the claims service runs a fraud model on it. claims the model scores as high risk go to the special investigations unit, the rest go to an adjuster. the adjuster asks the customer for photos and if the photos are missing the adjuster chases the customer again. when the damage is under two thousand dollars the adjuster approves payment straight away, otherwise a senior adjuster has to sign off first. finance pays the approved claims and emails the customer a receipt. investigators who find fraud refer the claim to the police.

errors.detail: The 'Photos missing?' decision is checked from Customer, but the adjuster is the one who checks whether the photos are missing.
'Photos missing?' has no 'no' outcome. The adjuster instead goes to the damage check unconditionally, so the photos check never gates the next step.
'Damage under two thousand?' yes loops back to Adjuster instead of leading to the adjuster approving payment and passing it to Finance.
After the senior adjuster signs off, the edge points back to Adjuster instead of the approved claim going on to Finance for payment.
Finance has no incoming edge from the approval path, so the flow from approval to payment and receipt is disconnected.

There is no 'fraud found?' decision for the investigators. Every claim sent to the special investigations unit goes to the police, but the text says only claims where investigators find fraud are referred.
Finance -> 'Approved claims' uses a box that is not in the boxes list. The unused 'Receipt' box is also left dangling.

description: the stage manager calls the cue on headset and the lighting operator presses go on the console. the console sends the cue over the network to the dimmer racks, and there is a network switch in front of the dimmer racks. if a dimmer rack doesn't acknowledge the cue the console retries it twice, and if it still fails the operator switches to the backup console. the follow spot operators also listen to the stage manager and pick up the lead actor when the stage manager says so. at the end of the act the stage manager tells the house manager, who opens the bar.

errors.detail: The house manager never connects to the bar. The text says the house manager opens the bar, but there is no 'House Manager -> Bar' edge, so the flow dead-ends.

The retry loop is missing. The text says the console retries the cue twice and only then, if it still fails, the operator switches to the backup console. The diagram sends a miss straight to the Backup Console, with no retry back to the Console and no 'still fails?' decision.
The 'no' outcome of 'Dimmer Rack miss?' points back to Console. When the rack acknowledges, the cue is done and nothing is resent.
The Stage Manager's headset call is never linked to the Lighting Operator. 'Headset' dead-ends, so nothing shows the call leading to the operator pressing go.
The follow spot operators pick up the lead actor only when the stage manager says so. The diagram has no decision for this and draws the pickup as unconditional.

description: a beekeeper inspects each hive every week and records it in the hive log. if the beekeeper sees queen cells they split the colony into a new hive, otherwise they check the honey supers. supers that are more than eighty percent capped go to the extraction room, which spins them and sends the honey to the bottling line. the bottling line labels the jars only when the moisture reading is under eighteen percent; wetter honey goes back to the extraction room to dry. a distributor collects the labelled jars on fridays.

errors.detail: The 'yes' outcome of 'Moisture under 18%?' loops back to Bottling Line instead of leading to the labelling of jars (labelled jars), so labelling never happens in the flow.
The Distributor collects from Hive, but the text says the distributor collects the labelled jars from the bottling line output, not from the hive.

description: the passenger books a ferry ticket on the website, which asks the booking engine for a space on the sailing. the booking engine checks vehicle deck capacity and if the deck is full it puts the passenger on the waitlist, otherwise it holds a space and sends the passenger to payment. if the payment fails the booking engine releases the space. the waitlist service watches for cancellations and offers freed spaces to waitlisted passengers by sms. on the day the port gate scans the ticket and lets the car board unless the ticket is for a different sailing, in which case the gate sends the driver to the ticket office.

errors.detail: When payment fails, the booking engine releases the space, but the diagram has no 'release space' step. The 'yes' edge only loops back to Booking Engine.
'Payment failed?' is checked from Booking Engine instead of from Payment. Payment has no edge into the decision, so the payment outcome never feeds it.
The booking engine holding a space before sending the passenger to payment is not shown. The 'no' branch goes straight to Payment.
The edges Waitlist -> Passenger 'notifies' and Payment -> Passenger 'notifies' are not in the text. The passenger is put on the waitlist and sent to payment, not notified.
The edge Booking Engine -> Sailing labeled 'routes to' misstates the relation. The booking engine is asked for a space on the sailing, and nothing is routed.

The waitlist service watches for cancellations and offers the freed spaces. The diagram shows it watching the Waitlist, with no cancellation or freed-space step. Port Gate also has no link to the passenger's ticket.

description: a clinic refers a patient to the clinical trial, and the research nurse screens them against the eligibility criteria. ineligible patients are referred back to the clinic. eligible patients sign a consent form, and the randomisation system assigns them to the drug arm or the placebo arm. the pharmacy dispenses the blinded kit for whichever arm they're in. every two weeks the nurse records side effects and if a side effect is serious the nurse reports it to the safety board within a day. the safety board can unblind the patient, and if the drug caused it the board stops the patient's treatment.

errors.detail: The screening flow is disconnected. Clinical Trial has no edge to Research Nurse, and nothing links the nurse's screening to the Ineligible? or Eligible? decisions, which have no incoming edges.
The eligibility decision has missing outcome paths. Ineligible? has no 'no' edge leading on to Eligible?/consent, and Eligible? has no 'no' outcome.
When the drug caused the reaction, the diagram points Adverse Reaction? at Patient. The text says the board stops the patient's treatment, and there is no stop-treatment box.

'Side Effect serious?' is used in edges but is not in the boxes list. The nurse's step of recording side effects is also absent, and the nurse's report to the safety board is only implied through the decision.
The safety board's unblinding of the patient is drawn as an edge to the cause decision. The decision 'drug caused it?' is named Adverse Reaction? and has no 'no' path.
The recurring side-effect recording every two weeks is not shown. A non-serious side effect has no 'no' path that returns to the next recording.
The pharmacy's dispensing of the blinded kit is drawn only as edges to the arms, with no kit box and no link to the patient. The within-a-day reporting limit is also missing.

description: trucks tip mixed recycling onto the intake belt, which carries it past a magnet that pulls out steel cans into the steel bay. the remaining material goes to an optical sorter which blows plastic bottles onto the plastics belt and lets paper fall through to the paper baler. a quality inspector watches the plastics belt and throws any paper back onto the intake belt. if the paper baler jams the line supervisor stops the intake belt until a mechanic clears it. full bales go to the loading dock where a buyer's truck collects them.

errors.detail: The remaining material after the magnet goes to the optical sorter, but the diagram sends it from Steel Bay to Optical Sorter instead of from Magnet, so the steel bay wrongly feeds the sorter.
The line supervisor stopping the intake belt when the paper baler jams is missing. There is no Line Supervisor box and no edge that stops the intake belt.
The mechanic clears the paper baler jam, but the diagram draws Mechanic routing to Intake Belt, which does not show the jam being cleared or the belt being stopped.
Full bales go from the paper baler to the loading dock, but there is no edge from Paper Baler to Loading Dock. The flow dead-ends at the baler and Loading Dock is unreachable.

The edge between Loading Dock and Buyer's Truck is drawn as the dock pointing to the truck, whereas the buyer's truck collects the bales from the dock. This is a passive relation drawn in the opposite direction.

description: a player clicks find match and the client sends the request to the matchmaker. the matchmaker looks for players within one hundred rating points, and if it can't find nine others within thirty seconds it widens the range and searches again. once ten players are found the matchmaker asks the server allocator for a game server, and if no server is free in the player's region the allocator falls back to the nearest region. the game server loads the map and the clients connect to it. there's an anti-cheat service in front of the game server that kicks any client that fails its check. when the match ends the game server sends results to the rating service, which updates every player's rating.

errors.detail: The 'Within 30 seconds?' yes edge goes back to Player (then Player to Matchmaker) instead of the matchmaker widening the range and searching again, so the retry loop is wrong.
The 'Ten players found?' decision has no 'no' outcome, so nothing happens when fewer than ten players are found. The 'Found nine?' yes path is also missing.
'Server free?' yes goes to Anti-cheat, but a free server should lead to the Game server being allocated.
The fallback to the nearest region dead-ends at 'Region'. It never leads to allocating a game server.

Anti-cheat is not placed in front of the Game server. There is no client-to-anti-cheat edge and no 'routes to' edge from anti-cheat to the game server. The edge showing clients connecting to the game server is also missing, and the map-loading edge points from the game server to the client.
There is no 'Fails check?' decision. Anti-cheat kicks every client unconditionally instead of only those that fail the check.
The Rating service has no outgoing edge, so updating every player's rating is missing and the flow dead-ends.
The 'Find match' box is orphaned and not connected to anything. The extra Player to Matchmaker 'sends request' edge duplicates the client's request.

description: the avalanche forecaster reads the overnight snow sensors every morning and rates the danger from one to five. when the rating is three or below the ski patrol opens the slopes as normal, the rest of the time the forecaster asks the patrol leader for a control mission. the patrol leader checks the weather and only if visibility is good does the helicopter fly the explosives team up, otherwise the mission waits an hour and the patrol leader checks again. after the blasts the team inspects each slope, and slopes that slid cleanly reopen while the others stay closed. the patrol leader reports every closure back to the forecaster.

errors.detail: When the rating is three or below, Ski Patrol points at Overnight Snow Sensors. The text says the patrol opens the slopes as normal, so the edge should go to the slopes (opens).
The 'slid cleanly' yes branch sends Slopes back to Overnight Snow Sensors with 'routes to'. The text says those slopes reopen, so this edge should show a reopening.

The path for slopes that did not slide cleanly (they stay closed) is missing. 'Slopes slid?' has no 'no' edge and is not listed in boxes. The Closure box has no incoming edge, so the patrol leader's closure report is never tied to the closed slopes.
The one-hour wait before the patrol leader rechecks the weather is not shown. The 'no' branch loops straight back to Patrol Leader.

An unconditional 'asks' edge from Avalanche Forecaster to Patrol Leader bypasses the rating decision. The text says the forecaster asks only when the rating is above three, and the 'no' branch already covers that.

description: a donor gives blood at the mobile clinic and the courier takes the bag to the blood bank. the lab tests every bag for infections and discards any bag that tests positive, the clean ones get separated into plasma and red cells. red cells go to the cold store and plasma goes to the freezer. when a hospital orders blood the dispatcher picks the oldest matching unit from the cold store, and on a miss it falls back to the regional blood bank. the dispatcher sends the unit by courier and the hospital confirms receipt.

errors.detail: Nothing connects the Blood Bank to the Lab, so the bag never reaches testing and the Lab has no incoming edge.
The 'Positive?' yes branch goes to Plasma, but a positive bag should be discarded. There is no discard box.
Clean bags are not separated into both plasma and red cells. Only the 'no' branch goes to Red Cells, and Plasma is reachable only from the positive branch.
The edge Cold Store -> Red Cells ('goes to') is not in the text. It reverses the flow and creates a cycle.
There is no 'cold store miss' decision. The Dispatcher goes to the regional Blood Bank unconditionally instead of only when the cold store has no matching unit.
The Dispatcher sends the unit straight to the Hospital. The text says it goes by courier, so the Courier step is missing.

description: each morning the vineyard manager samples grapes from every block and measures the sugar. blocks above twenty four brix get picked that day, the others are sampled again tomorrow. the pickers load the grapes into bins and a tractor hauls the bins to the crush pad. at the crush pad the sorting table removes leaves and rotten bunches, and the destemmer sends the clean fruit to the fermentation tanks. the winemaker tastes each tank daily and if fermentation stalls she adds yeast, else she leaves it until it's dry.

errors.detail: The 'Today' outcome dead-ends: blocks above 24 brix are picked that day, but 'Today' is not connected to the Pickers, so the harvest flow never starts from the decision.
Blocks at or below 24 brix are sampled again tomorrow, but 'Tomorrow' does not loop back to the sampling step (Vineyard Manager / Block) and dead-ends.
The step where the winemaker adds yeast when fermentation stalls is absent. The 'yes' branch just points back at Fermentation Tanks.
The 'no' outcome of 'Fermentation stalls?' points back to Winemaker, but the text says she leaves the tank until it is dry, so a 'leave until dry' outcome is missing.

description: the dentist scans the patient's tooth and uploads the scan to the dental lab portal. the portal queues it for a designer, who models the crown and sends the design back to the dentist for approval. if the dentist asks for changes the designer reworks it, otherwise the design goes to the milling machine. the milling machine cuts the crown from a zirconia block and the furnace sinters it. a technician checks the fit on a printed model and anything that doesn't fit goes back to the milling machine, the rest are shipped to the dentist.

errors.detail: The 'Changes needed?' decision is checked by the Designer (edge Designer -> Changes needed?), but the dentist reviews the design and asks for changes, so the check should come from the Dentist.
'Reworks it' is a dead end. The text says the designer reworks the design, which should loop back to the Designer and then to the dentist for approval.

There is no flow from the Milling Machine to the Furnace, or from the Furnace to the Technician. The Furnace only points at the Zirconia Block, and the Technician has no incoming edge, so the cut, sinter and fit-check sequence is broken.
The fit decision is checked from 'Printed Model' rather than the Technician, who is the one checking the fit.
The 'Crown' box is unused and disconnected, and the Furnace -> Zirconia Block edge makes the furnace sinter the block rather than the cut crown.

description: a broadcaster uploads a film to the subtitling platform, which sends the audio to the speech recogniser. the recogniser produces a draft transcript and a translator corrects it and translates it. a reviewer watches the film with the subtitles and returns any scene with timing errors to the translator. once the reviewer signs off the platform burns the subtitles into a preview, and only when the broadcaster approves the preview does the platform deliver the final files. rejected previews go back to the reviewer.

errors.detail: The Speech Recogniser's draft transcript goes straight to the Reviewer. The text sends it to the Translator, who corrects and translates it, so the Translator has no incoming edge.
There is no edge from the Translator to the Reviewer, so the reviewer never receives the translated subtitles. The timing-error loop back to the Translator also dead-ends.
There is no 'Broadcaster approves?' decision. Final Files is only delivered by the platform on a 'yes', yet the Final Files box has no incoming edge.

The edge 'Preview -> Broadcaster: delivers final files' is wrong. The platform delivers the final files after approval, and the broadcaster is not the recipient of that step. The extra 'Broadcaster -> Subtitling Platform: approves' edge is not tied to any decision.
The 'Rejected previews?' decision is checked from Preview, but the Broadcaster is the one who approves or rejects the preview.
The platform's step of burning subtitles into the preview is missing. The Reviewer connects directly to Preview, and the 'no timing errors' branch is not drawn as a decision outcome.

description: a reader emails the newspaper about a mistake and the email lands in the corrections inbox. the standards editor reads it and asks the reporter who wrote the story whether it's wrong. if the reporter agrees the standards editor writes a correction, if not the editor checks the source documents herself. corrections for print stories go to the night desk for tomorrow's paper, the rest are added to the web article straight away. the standards editor replies to the reader either way.

errors.detail: No edge from the Corrections Inbox to the Standards Editor, so the step where the standards editor reads the email is missing and the flow dead-ends at the inbox.

There is no 'Reporter agrees?' decision box with yes/no outcomes. 'agrees?' is used as an edge label from Standards Editor to Reporter, so the yes branch (standards editor writes a correction) and the no branch are not drawn.
The 'Standards Editor writes a correction' step is absent, so nothing produces the correction that later goes to the night desk or the web article.

The 'no' outcome (the standards editor checks the source documents herself) is not drawn. The diagram sends the Reporter to a separate 'Editor' box, which then loops back to the Standards Editor with 'checks'.
The edge Reporter -> Corrections Inbox 'writes for' is not in the text. The reporter does not write for the inbox, and the edge distorts the flow.
The separate 'Editor' box duplicates the Standards Editor ('the editor ... herself') and the Reporter -> Editor 'writes for' edge is invented.
There is no 'Print story?' decision box. Night Desk and Web Article are both attached to the inbox without a yes/no split, so the print-versus-rest routing is lost.
Night Desk and Web Article edges start at the Corrections Inbox, but the corrections that go there are the ones the standards editor has written.

description: customers upload models to the print farm website and the slicer turns each model into print instructions. the scheduler sends jobs to the printers, there are twelve printers and the scheduler uses least connections. a camera watches every print and if it spots spaghetti it cancels the job and the scheduler requeues it. finished prints go to the post processing bench where a worker removes supports. prints that need painting go to the paint booth first, the others go straight to packing, and the courier collects from packing at five.

errors.detail: The Slicer has no edge to the Scheduler, so the print instructions never reach the scheduler and the flow dead-ends after slicing.
The edge 'turns model' runs from Slicer to Print Farm Website, but the website should hand the uploaded model to the Slicer.

The 'Spaghetti?' decision is reused for the painting choice. Printer feeds it directly, and its yes/no go to Paint Booth and Packing, so the paint routing is attached to the wrong question and the wrong checker.
There is no 'needs painting?' decision after the Post Processing Bench. The bench has no outgoing edges, so prints never go from the bench to the Paint Booth or to Packing.
The Worker box is not connected to anything. The edge showing the worker removing supports at the Post Processing Bench is missing.

description: the pilot requests pushback from ground control, which checks the departure queue. if the queue is longer than ten aircraft ground control holds the pilot at the gate, otherwise it clears the pushback. the pilot taxis to the runway holding point and switches to the tower. the tower clears the aircraft for takeoff unless another aircraft is on final approach, in which case the pilot waits and asks again. after takeoff the tower hands the aircraft to departure control.

errors.detail: The retry edge 'asks again' goes from Pilot to Departure Queue, but the text says the pilot waits and asks the tower again for takeoff clearance, so it should point back to Tower.

description: each turbine streams vibration data to the monitoring centre, where a wear model scores it. turbines with a high score get a maintenance ticket, the others keep running. the planner looks at the ticket and the wind forecast, and crews only climb when the wind is below twelve metres per second, otherwise the planner reschedules the ticket for the next calm day. the crew replaces the worn part and records it in the asset system. if the turbine still vibrates after the restart the crew calls the manufacturer's engineer.

errors.detail: The 'Score high?' decision is fed by Turbine, but the wear model in the monitoring centre scores the data and decides, so the edge should come from Wear Model.
'Score high?' has no 'no' outcome. The text says turbines without a high score keep running, and that path is absent.

The crew replacing the worn part and the turbine restart are not shown as steps or as edges back to Turbine. The vibration check follows directly from Crews, though the text puts it after the restart.

description: a caller dials the emergency line and the call taker asks the triage questions. the triage software gives a priority, and priority one calls go straight to the nearest ambulance while lower priorities wait in the queue for a free crew. if no ambulance is free within eight minutes for a priority one call the dispatcher sends a fire engine as first responder. the crew treats the patient on scene and decides whether they need hospital. patients who don't are discharged at home, the others are taken to the emergency department, which the crew pre-alerts by radio.

errors.detail: Emergency Line has no edge to Call Taker, so the call taker never receives the call and the intake flow is broken.
There is no 'Priority one?' decision from the triage result, and Triage Questions only connects to Priority One. Priority Two has no incoming edge, so lower-priority calls never reach the queue.
The 'no ambulance free within eight minutes' check for priority one is absent. Dispatcher has no incoming edge and Fire Engine leads nowhere, so the fire-engine fallback is not connected to the flow.
Ambulance goes straight to the 'Patient stable?' decision, skipping the crew treating the patient on scene. Scene Crew has no incoming edge.
The hospital decision is checked by Ambulance (and Emergency Department) instead of the Scene Crew. Scene Crew instead has a plain 'decides' edge to Hospital.
The decision polarity is swapped: 'Patient stable?' yes goes to the Emergency Department and no goes to Home. Stable patients should be discharged and unstable ones taken to hospital.

The edges 'Emergency Department → Patient stable?', 'Patient stable? → Emergency Line' and 'Emergency Line → Dispatcher (pre-alerts)' are not in the text. The crew should pre-alert the Emergency Department by radio.
The Home (discharged at home) box is used in an edge but is not in the box list, so the no-hospital outcome is not properly represented.
Free Crew is a dead end. The queued calls never lead to an ambulance or crew being dispatched and then treating the patient.

description: parents apply online and the council's admissions system checks the home address. children inside the catchment get a place offer from the school, everyone else goes on the waiting list ranked by distance. parents have two weeks to accept, and offers that aren't accepted in time are withdrawn and given to the next child on the waiting list. accepted offers go to the school office, which sends the welcome pack. parents who are refused can appeal to the independent panel, and if the panel upholds the appeal the school has to offer a place.

errors.detail: There is no 'inside the catchment?' decision after the home address check. Home Address is a dead end, and the yes path (place offer from the school) and no path (waiting list) are not branched from it.

The edges School -> Waiting List ('offers place' and the duplicate 'offers offer') and Waiting List -> Home Address ('routes to') are not in the text. They tangle the catchment outcomes and wrongly send the waiting list back to the address check.
The school's place offer never reaches the 'Accepted in time?' decision. That decision hangs off Parents, so the offer-then-accept sequence is not drawn.

A withdrawn offer should go to the next child on the waiting list, who then receives the offer and goes through acceptance. Next Child is a dead end with no link to Waiting List or back to the offer or acceptance step.

'Refused?' is checked by Parents, but the refusal is a decision by the admissions system or school. The refused-to-appeal path is not tied to the outcome of the admissions decision, so waiting-list children are not linked to it.
'School' appears twice as a box, and the appeal-upheld edge goes to the duplicate rather than a single School box.

description: a taxpayer files a return through the tax portal, which runs it through the validation engine. returns with errors are sent back to the taxpayer to fix, and the rest go to the risk scorer. low risk returns are paid automatically by the treasury system, anything above that waits for a case officer. the case officer asks the taxpayer for receipts and if they don't arrive within thirty days the officer rejects the refund. otherwise the officer approves it and the treasury system pays it.

errors.detail: The case officer asking the taxpayer for receipts is not drawn. There is no edge from Case Officer to Taxpayer, so the receipts check has no source.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Receipts missing?' goes to a generic 'Refund' box. The text says the officer rejects the refund, so it needs a rejection step.
'Receipts missing?' has no 'no' branch. The text says that if receipts arrive the officer approves the refund. Approval is instead drawn as an unconditional edge from Case Officer.

The approval path is wrong. A duplicate 'Officer' box is added and approval skips the decision. The edge between Treasury System and Officer points the wrong way, since approval should lead to Treasury System paying the refund.

description: the courier scans a parcel at the locker bank and the locker controller looks for a free compartment of the right size. if there isn't one the courier takes the parcel back to the depot, otherwise the controller opens the door and the courier drops the parcel in. the controller texts the recipient a pickup code. a recipient who doesn't collect within three days gets a reminder, and after five days the controller flags the parcel for return and the courier picks it up on the next round.

errors.detail: 'Compartment free?' has no 'no' outcome. The text says the courier takes the parcel back to the depot when no compartment is free.
The 'yes' edge from 'Compartment free?' loops back to Locker Bank. The text says the controller opens the door and the courier drops the parcel in.
The 'Door open?' decision, checked by the Courier, is not in the text. It also carries the depot path that belongs to the compartment check.
The courier dropping the parcel into the compartment is not shown as a step. Only a Controller to Courier 'opens' edge exists.
The reminder sent to the recipient after three days without collection is absent. The 'Recipient overdue?' yes branch has no outgoing edge.
The Recipient feeds the overdue and return decisions, but the controller is the one that tracks the days, sends reminders and flags the parcel.
The flow ends at the 'flags for' edge into Courier. The courier picking the parcel up on the next round and returning it is not shown as a step.

description: the shot firer loads the blast holes and wires them to the firing box. before every blast the site supervisor sweeps the exclusion zone and the blast only goes ahead when the zone is clear, if anyone is inside the supervisor sounds the siren and sweeps again. the shot firer fires the blast and waits fifteen minutes for fumes. then he inspects the face for misfires, and any misfired hole is reported to the mine manager who decides whether to refire it. after the all clear the loader moves in to dig the broken rock.

errors.detail: The 'yes' outcome of 'Zone clear?' points to Exclusion Zone, but when the zone is clear the blast goes ahead, so it should lead to the shot firer firing the blast.
There is no 'fires the blast' step. The shot firer goes straight to waiting for fumes, and the loading/wiring steps are never connected to the supervisor's sweep.
After the siren the supervisor sweeps again, but the Siren edge goes to Exclusion Zone, which has no edge back to 'Zone clear?', so the re-sweep and re-check loop is not closed.
Fumes has no edge to Inspect Face, so the face inspection is disconnected from the wait and the flow dead-ends after the fumes wait.
The 'no' outcome of 'Misfire?' is missing. With no misfire the process should proceed to the all clear and the loader.
There is no decision box for whether the mine manager refires the hole (a 'Refire?' yes/no). The mine manager's decision is reduced to a single edge.
Mine Manager 'refires' points to Exclusion Zone instead of the misfired hole or the firing step, so the refire path is wrong. The no-refire path is also absent.
Nothing leads into Loader (no all-clear step after inspection or refire). Loader moves in to Exclusion Zone instead of digging the broken rock, which is not represented.
The supervisor's sweep of the exclusion zone is not drawn as an action, because Site Supervisor has no edge to Exclusion Zone.

description: the brewer mashes the grain and the wort goes to the kettle for the boil. the chiller cools the wort into the fermenter and the brewer pitches yeast. the lab takes a gravity reading every day and the beer moves to the conditioning tank only once the gravity stops dropping, until then it stays in the fermenter. from conditioning the beer is filtered and goes either to the canning line or the keg filler, depending on the order. any can that the fill checker finds underfilled is kicked off the line.

errors.detail: There is no edge from Kettle to Chiller, so the boiled wort never reaches the chiller and the chain from kettle to fermenter is broken.
Yeast is pitched but never connected to the Fermenter, so the pitching step dead-ends.
The choice between the canning line and the keg filler 'depending on the order' has no decision box. Filter goes to both unconditionally.
The 'Underfilled?' decision has no incoming edge from Fill Checker. It points to Fill Checker with 'yes', so the checker is not the one making the decision.
Canning Line is not connected to Fill Checker, so cans are never checked after filling and the underfilled check is disconnected from the main flow.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Underfilled?' leads to Fill Checker instead of to the kick-off step. The kick-off edge comes from Fill Checker directly, bypassing the decision.

description: a doping control officer collects a urine sample from the athlete and splits it into an a bottle and a b bottle. both bottles go to the accredited lab. the lab tests the a sample and negative results are reported to the federation and closed. if the a sample is positive the federation notifies the athlete, who can ask for the b sample to be tested. when the b sample confirms it the federation suspends the athlete, otherwise the case is dropped.

errors.detail: 'Sample positive?' is checked from Federation, but the lab tests the A sample and produces the result, so the edge should come from the lab.
'Sample negative?' has no 'no' outcome. A positive A sample should lead on to the federation notifying the athlete, but the diagram routes the negative report to the positive check instead.
The negative result is reported to the federation but the case is never closed.

'Bottle positive?' is checked from Federation directly. It should follow the lab testing the B bottle after the athlete asks, so the B test is bypassed and the athlete's request does not feed into it.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Bottle positive?' goes to Athlete, and the suspension edge runs Athlete→Federation, which reverses the relation. The federation should suspend the athlete when B confirms.
There is no 'no' outcome for 'Bottle positive?', so the described 'otherwise the case is dropped' path is absent.
Athlete appears twice as a duplicate box.

description: a client sends a document to the translation agency's project manager, who gets a quote from the pricing tool. if the client accepts the quote the project manager assigns a translator, else the request is archived. the translator works in the cat tool, which checks every segment against the translation memory and fills in exact matches automatically. a proofreader checks the finished translation and sends anything with errors back to the translator. the project manager delivers the final file and the billing team invoices the client.

errors.detail: The client's document goes to a 'Translation Agency' box instead of the Project Manager, so the Project Manager has no incoming flow and the process is disconnected at the start.

There is no edge from the Translator (or Cat Tool) to the Proofreader, and the Proofreader's 'checks' edge points to a 'Finished translation' box that does not exist in the boxes list, so the work never reaches the proofreader.

The proofreader's 'errors?' decision is missing. The path where the translation has no errors and goes on to the Project Manager is also missing. The Proofreader only sends work back to the Translator.
The Project Manager 'delivers file' to the Billing Team, but the text says the final file is delivered to the client. The delivery to the Client is missing.

description: each elevator reports faults to the remote monitoring service. the service tries to reset the elevator remotely, and if the reset works it logs the fault and does nothing else. when the reset fails it raises a call with the maintenance dispatcher, who sends the nearest technician. if someone is trapped inside the dispatcher also calls the fire brigade. the technician repairs the elevator and the monitoring service watches it for an hour before closing the call.

errors.detail: Logs Fault flows on to 'Reset failed?', but the text says that after a successful reset the service logs the fault and does nothing else.
'Reset succeeded?' has no 'no' edge to the Maintenance Dispatcher. The escalation instead hangs off a redundant 'Reset failed?' box that is only reached through the success path.
'Nearest Technician' dead-ends and is not linked to the separate 'Technician' box that repairs the elevator. The dispatch-to-repair chain is broken.
The monitoring service 'watches' the Technician, but the text says it watches the elevator after the repair. Nothing orders the watch after the repair either.
There is no step for closing the call after the one-hour watch, so the process never reaches its end.

description: a skier books skis online and the rental system reserves a pair in their size at the shop. at the shop the technician adjusts the bindings to the skier's weight and the skier signs the waiver. skis come back at the end of the day through the return counter, where staff check them for damage. damaged skis go to the repair bench, the rest are waxed and put back on the rack. if the repair bench can't fix them the shop manager writes them off.

errors.detail: The 'Damaged?' decision is checked by Skier, but the text says staff at the return counter check the skis for damage, so the edge should come from Staff.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Repair failed?' goes to Staff, but the text says the shop manager writes the skis off. There is no Shop Manager or write-off box.
The skier signs the waiver, but the diagram has a 'Weight' box that the skier 'signs'. The waiver is missing and the edge targets the wrong thing.
Undamaged skis are waxed before going back on the rack, but there is no waxing step between 'Damaged?' and 'Rack'.

The edge from Technician to Skier, labeled 'adjusts to', and the edge from Rental System to Shop, labeled 'routes to', are not described this way. The technician adjusts the bindings to the skier's weight, and the system reserves skis at the shop.

description: farmers send seed samples to the seed bank, where a technician cleans and counts them. the technician runs a germination test, and samples that germinate below eighty five percent are sent back to the farmer for a fresh sample. good samples are dried to five percent moisture and sealed in foil bags. the bags go to the minus twenty vault. every ten years the curator retests a portion of each sample, and if germination has dropped the curator asks the regeneration field to grow fresh seed.

errors.detail: Dried samples are fed from Farmers (sends samples) instead of from the passing branch of the germination check, so good samples never flow from the test to drying.

The germination check is split into a 'Germination test?' box and an 'Eighty-five percent?' box chained by a 'no' edge. The text has one decision (germination below 85%), so this chain scrambles the yes/no outcomes.
The Curator's retest feeds the same 'Germination test?' decision the technician uses. The curator's check (has germination dropped?) should be its own decision box.
'Germination test?' yes goes to Regeneration field, so the technician's initial test can trigger regrowth. Regrowth should only follow the curator's retest finding that germination dropped.

The ten-year retest is not connected to the stored samples (vault to Curator). The Curator is disconnected from the flow, and there is no explicit 'germination dropped?' decision with a yes path to the Regeneration field.
The drying step omits the five percent moisture target, and the Regeneration field's fresh seed is not linked back to the process.

description: sewage arrives at the treatment works and passes through the screens, which remove rags into a skip. the grit channel settles out sand and the flow goes on to the primary tanks. the aeration lanes treat the water next, and there are four lanes using round robin. a turbidity sensor sits in front of the river outfall and diverts any cloudy water back to the aeration lanes. sludge from the primary tanks is pumped to the digester, which makes biogas for the generator.

errors.detail: No edge leads from Screens to the Grit Channel, so the flow dead-ends at the Skip and the Grit Channel has no input.
The edge between Aeration Lanes and Primary Tanks points the wrong way. Water flows from the Primary Tanks to the Aeration Lanes.
Nothing connects the Aeration Lanes to the Turbidity Sensor. The treated water never reaches the sensor that sits in front of the outfall.
There is no decision box such as 'Cloudy water?'. Cloudy water should go back to the Aeration Lanes and clear water should go on to the River Outfall.

The diversion back to the Aeration Lanes starts at the River Outfall, and the sensor only points at the outfall. The sensor should be the one sending cloudy water back, and the sensor should take over the edges into the outfall, with a 'routes to' edge to it.
The Primary Tanks pass flow on to the Aeration Lanes but that edge is missing, and the Grit Channel's output into the Primary Tanks is the only inbound path shown.

description: a steward finds a lost item and hands it to the lost and found desk. the desk logs it in the property system and anything valuable goes into the safe. when a fan reports a lost item online the property system searches for a match. on a match the desk emails the fan to collect it, and on a miss the system keeps the report open for thirty days. unclaimed items are given to charity after ninety days, except phones, which the desk wipes and recycles.

errors.detail: The steward hands the item to the 'Lost and Found' box, which is separate from 'Desk'. The text says the steward hands it to the lost and found desk, which is the Desk that logs it, so the flow is disconnected.
The edge Desk -> Lost and Found 'gives item' is invented. The text says unclaimed items go to charity, not back to a lost and found box.

The fan's online report is drawn as Property System -> Fan 'searches for match' and Fan -> Online. The fan should report online and that report should reach the Property System, which then searches. Nothing connects the report to the Property System.
'Match?' is checked by the Desk. The Property System does the search, so it should check the match.

The match 'yes' outcome goes straight to Fan. The text says the desk emails the fan, and no Desk email step appears. The 'no' outcome loops through the Property System rather than going directly to the report being kept open for thirty days.

The phone exception is placed after 'Unclaimed? no'. Unclaimed items should go to the phone check, with phones wiped and recycled and non-phones given to charity. The diagram sends all unclaimed items to Charity and only reaches 'Phone?' when the item is not unclaimed.
The 'Phone?' no outcome has no edge. Non-phone unclaimed items should go to Charity.
There is no recycle step. Wipe -> Desk 'recycles' loops back to the Desk instead of leading to recycling, so the phone path never ends correctly.
'Anything valuable goes into the safe' is a conditional, but it is drawn as an unconditional Desk -> Safe edge with no decision box. The ninety-day wait before charity is also missing.

description: a family fills in an adoption form at the shelter and the adoption counsellor reviews it. families with a garden and no other dogs move straight to a meet and greet, the rest get a home visit first. if the home visit fails the counsellor declines the application. at the meet and greet the behaviourist watches the dog with the family, and only if the behaviourist is happy does the family pay the fee. the vet microchips the dog before it goes home.

errors.detail: The garden/no-other-dogs decision is checked from Family, but the adoption counsellor reviews the form and sends families on to the meet and greet or the home visit.
The decision is named only 'Dog-free?' and drops the garden condition, so the garden-and-no-other-dogs test is not fully represented.
'Home visit fails?' hangs off the Adoption counsellor, and the Home visit box has no edge into it, so the home visit's result is never what is checked.
A failed home visit loops back to Adoption counsellor instead of leading to a decline-application outcome.
There is no path for a passed home visit leading on to the meet and greet.
'Behaviourist happy?' is checked from Meet and greet, but the behaviourist makes this judgement. The behaviourist watching the dog with the family is not part of the meet and greet flow.
There is no 'family pays the fee' step, and the 'yes' outcome of 'Behaviourist happy?' goes to Behaviourist instead of to the fee payment.
Vet microchips the Behaviourist, which is nonsensical. The vet should microchip the dog, after payment and before the dog goes home.
The dog and the dog going home are absent, and the microchipping step is not connected after the fee payment.

description: an advertiser books a radio spot through the sales rep, who checks the traffic system for free slots. if the slot is taken the rep offers the next free slot, and the advertiser either takes it or cancels. the creative team records the ad and legal reviews the script. ads that make health claims need sign off from the compliance manager. the traffic system then schedules the ad into the playout system, which plays it and sends a proof of play to billing.

errors.detail: Both the 'yes' and 'no' outcomes of 'Slot taken?' go to 'Next Free Slot'. The 'no' (slot free) path should continue to the ad production and scheduling steps instead.
There is an extra edge from Advertiser to 'Slot taken?'. The sales rep checks the slot, not the advertiser, and the rep's own edge already covers this.

The advertiser's choice after the next free slot is offered (take it or cancel) is missing. 'Next Free Slot' dead-ends with no accept/cancel decision, no path to continue if taken, and no cancel outcome.

The creative team and legal edges are wrong. 'Creative Team' points to 'Advertiser' and 'Legal' points to 'Creative Team'. The creative team should record the ad and then legal should review the script, as part of the booking flow.
There is no 'Health claims?' decision. The compliance sign-off is drawn as an unconditional edge from Advertiser, and non-health ads have no path that skips it.
Compliance Manager is a dead end. After sign-off, and after legal review for ads without health claims, the flow never reaches the Traffic System to schedule the ad.
The edge from Advertiser to Compliance Manager ('needs sign off') is not described. The sign-off applies to ads with health claims and comes after legal review, not from the advertiser.

description: the archivist pulls a box of letters and the conservator checks each letter's condition. fragile letters go to the conservation studio to be repaired first, the others go straight to the scanning room. the scanner operator scans each letter and the ocr service extracts the text. pages where the ocr confidence is low go to volunteers to transcribe by hand. the catalogue publishes the scans with the text and the archivist returns the box to the stacks.

errors.detail: There is no 'Fragile?' decision box; the Conservator goes to both the Conservation Studio and the Scanning Room with unlabeled edges, so the fragile/other split is lost.
After repair, the Conservation Studio loops back to the Conservator, but the text says repaired letters continue to the scanning room.
The Scanning Room has no edge to the Scanner Operator, so the flow dead-ends there and the scanning step is disconnected.
The edge from OCR Service back to Conservator is not in the text and creates a loop that doesn't exist.
The 'Low confidence?' decision has no 'no' outcome, so pages with acceptable OCR confidence never go on to the Catalogue.
Volunteers have no outgoing edge, so hand transcription never feeds the Catalogue. The Catalogue has no incoming edges at all, so the scans and text never reach publication.
'Text' is drawn as a separate box that the Catalogue 'publishes' to, rather than the Catalogue publishing the scans together with the text from OCR or volunteers.

description: green beans arrive from the importer and the quality lab roasts a small sample. if the sample cups below eighty points the roastery returns the lot to the importer. accepted lots go to the warehouse until the head roaster schedules them. the roaster drops each batch into the cooling tray and the colour meter reads it, and batches outside the target colour are sold as seconds. good batches rest for two days, then the packing machine bags them and the web shop ships orders.

errors.detail: The edge "Quality Lab" -> "Importer" (roasts sample) is wrong: the lab roasts a sample of the arriving green beans, so the lot should flow into the Quality Lab and the Importer should not be its target.
The "Sample under 80?" decision has no "no" branch, so accepted lots never go to the Warehouse.

The Warehouse and Head Roaster edges are wrong. The text says lots wait in the warehouse until the head roaster schedules them, so the flow should be Warehouse -> Head Roaster -> roasting. The diagram instead has Roastery -> Head Roaster -> Warehouse, and the Warehouse is a dead end.
Roasting and the Cooling Tray hang off the Roastery, which is only reached by rejected lots. Batches should come from the scheduled, accepted lots, so the main flow is disconnected from acceptance.
The "Off Target?" decision has no "no" branch, so good batches never go on to rest and then reach the Packing Machine.
The two-day rest of good batches before packing is not represented.
The edge "Packing Machine" -> "Warehouse" (bags batches) is not in the text. Packing takes good batches after resting, not from the Warehouse, and the Packing Machine has no valid incoming flow.

description: a drone flies along the bridge and photographs every girder. the photos go to a crack detection model, which flags any crack longer than five millimetres. the bridge engineer reviews the flagged photos and sends a rope access team for anything she can't judge from the photo. if the team or the engineer finds a serious crack the engineer closes a lane and orders a repair, otherwise the crack is added to the watch list. the drone rechecks watch list cracks every three months.

errors.detail: The 'Crack > 5 mm?' yes edge loops back to Crack detector. The flagged photos should go to the Bridge engineer for review, so the engineer never receives them.
There is no decision for whether the engineer can judge the photo. The engineer is shown sending every case to the rope team instead of only those she can't judge.

There is no 'Serious crack?' decision checked by the engineer after the rope team or her own review. The yes path (close lane, order repair) and the otherwise path (add to watch list) are not branched.
'Orders repair' points to Watch list. A repair should be its own step (a Repair box) that happens for serious cracks, while the watch list is for non-serious ones.
Rope team goes straight to Watch list. The team's findings should return to the engineer's serious-crack decision, where a serious crack leads to a lane closure and repair.
The box 'Inspection every 3 months' is disconnected and redundant. The recheck is already shown by the Drone-to-Watch list edge.

description: the launch director polls each console for a go. propulsion, range safety and weather all report to the director. if any console says no go the director holds the count, fixes the issue and polls again. on a full go the ground computer runs the terminal count. the flight computer takes over at ten seconds and aborts the launch on any sensor fault, otherwise it ignites the engines and releases the clamps.

errors.detail: The 'no' outcome of the console check (full go) has no edge to the Ground Computer, so the terminal count is never triggered.
Terminal Count dead-ends. Nothing hands over to the Flight Computer at ten seconds.
On a sensor fault the diagram goes to Clamps. The text says the launch is aborted, and there is no abort box.
The direct edges from Flight Computer to Clamps and to Engines ('ignites') skip the sensor fault decision. They imply ignition and clamp release happen regardless of a fault.
The no-fault path goes only to Engines. Releasing the clamps after ignition is not on that path.
The director's 'holds the count' step is missing before the issue is fixed.

description: teams submit their projects on the hackathon site, which checks the submission has a demo video. submissions without a video are marked incomplete and the site emails the team, who can resubmit until the deadline. complete submissions are split across judges using round robin. each judge scores the project and projects with a big score gap between judges go to the head judge to break the tie. the organisers announce the top three from the final scores.

errors.detail: The 'Demo video?' yes edge loops back to Hackathon Site instead of sending the complete submission on to be split across the judges.
'Demo video?' has no 'no' outcome that marks the submission incomplete and emails the team.
The 'Submissions incomplete?' decision box is not in the text. The site checks the video, so incompleteness is the 'no' outcome of that check, but here it is checked unconditionally from the site.
The edge from Team to Judges (round robin) is invented. Incomplete submissions should not reach the judges, and judging should follow only the complete-submission path.
The resubmit loop goes from a duplicate 'Team' box to 'Teams', not back to the site's video check, and the deadline limit is missing.

There is no score-gap decision. Judges send everything to the Head Judge, and the path where projects without a big gap go straight to final scores is missing. The judges' scoring step is also absent.
The Organisers edge points at Head Judge ('announces from'). It should be the final scores leading to the Organisers announcing the top three, and the flow after the Head Judge dead-ends.

description: the manufacturer ships vaccine boxes with a temperature logger to the national store. the store manager reads the logger on arrival and quarantines any box that went above eight degrees, the rest go into the walk in fridge. district nurses order vaccines from the store every week and the store packs them in cool boxes with ice packs. at the clinic the nurse checks the vial monitor and only uses vials whose monitor hasn't changed colour. used vials are counted and the count goes back to the store manager for restocking.

errors.detail: The 'Over eight degrees?' yes branch goes to Walk In Fridge, but boxes above eight degrees are quarantined, not put in the fridge.
There is no Quarantine box, so the path for boxes that went above eight degrees is missing.
The 'no' branch points back to National Store instead of to the Walk In Fridge, where the remaining boxes go.
Cool Box has no outgoing edge. The packed vaccines never reach the district nurse or clinic, so the flow dead-ends.
The 'Vial Change?' decision has no yes outcome (vials that changed colour are not used). The no branch loops back to Vial Monitor instead of leading to using the vials.
No step for using the vials and no edge into Vial Count from used vials. The count is never produced, so the loop back to the store manager for restocking is disconnected.
Temperature Logger is drawn as a pass-through that 'routes to' National Store. The logger travels with the boxes, and the manufacturer ships to the store.
Vial Monitor and Vial Change? are each listed twice as duplicate boxes.
Ice packs are omitted, and the weekly ordering is not shown.
